land.text: the Gujarat plain governed from Patan by Zafar Khan for the Tughlaqs

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Declared independence from Delhi Sultanate: 1394'; the sultan's title from 1407.

land.text: Gujarat, annexed by Akbar in 1573 as the Gujarat Subah

successors.note: Bassein and Diu were Portuguese from 1534; Muzaffar Shah III raised revolts to 1584.

capitals.name: Anhilwad Patan (Patan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Anhilwad Patan (1407-1411)'; before 1407 the page is silent and the Tughlaq governor's seat is taken as Patan.

capitals.name: Ahmedabad
capitals.note: Founded 26 February 1411; chosen as capital 4 March 1411.

rulers.name: Mahmud Begada
rulers.note: His own page gives 18 June 1459 to 23 November 1511.

rulers.name: Muzaffar Shah III
rulers.note: A figurehead of the nobles; the table adds 1584 for his revolt.

correction.text: the Gujarat plain around Patan and Ahmedabad under Zafar Khan and Muzaffar Shah I, without the independent Champaner and Idar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Gujarat Sultanate row). The page gives no area and no boundary; 'Declared independence from Delhi Sultanate: 1394' and Anhilwad Patan as capital, so the core is the mainland of present Gujarat without Saurashtra, Kutch and the two Rajput kingdoms that Gujarat later conquered or subjected (Champaner 1484, Idar 1428). The extent is my reading of the later conquests listed on the page.

correction.text: the Gujarat mainland including Idar, which Ahmad Shah captured in November 1428; Champaner still independent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Ahmad Shah had to again attack and capture Idar in November 1428'; the ledger carries the gain.

correction.text: the mainland plus Thane and Mahim on the Konkan coast, annexed after the Konkan War (1429-1431)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Ahmad Shah annexed Thana and Mahim from Bahmani Sultanate'; the page gives no area.

correction.text: as before plus Junagadh (Girnar) in Sorath, conquered 1467-1470

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: infobox 'Conquest of Junagadh: 1467-1470'. The Mahmud Begada page has the siege of Junagadh at '1472-73', so the year is the Gujarat page's.

correction.text: as before plus Dwarka at the western tip of Saurashtra

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'On 14 May 1473, Sultan Mahmud marched with a large army against Dwarka'; 'The conquest and annexation of Junagarh, Dwarka, and Champaner extended the frontiers of the kingdom'.

correction.text: the whole Gujarat mainland with Champaner (Pavagadh, conquered 21 November 1484), Junagadh and Dwarka, and the Konkan coast of Thane and Mahim

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Pavagadh was conquered on 21 November 1484'. Sorath beyond Junagadh stays outside (the Bahadur Shah page: 'The whole of Gujarat, except Sorath' fell to Humayun in 1535).

correction.text: the Gujarat kingdom at its height: the mainland, Junagadh and Dwarka, Thane and Mahim, Malwa (Mandu fell 1531) and Raisen with Bhilsa and Chanderi under the governor of Malwa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Up to the defeat of Sultan Bahadur by Humayun, the power of Gujarat was at its height'; Malwa annexed after Mandu fell in 1531; Raisen captured 1531 and placed 'under the governor of Malwa'. Khandesh and Ahmadnagar acknowledged Bahadur as overlord (vassal tints, not territory).

correction.text: as 1531-1533 without Bassein, Bombay and Daman, ceded to Portugal by the Treaty of Bassein (23 December 1534)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Portuguese Empire gained control of the city of Bassein' and 'Bombay, Bassein and Daman would become a Portuguese colony' (Gujarat Sultanate page). Diu follows (ledger).

correction.text: the kingdom during Humayun's occupation of Gujarat and Malwa: shown hatched in the ledger's occupation; Sorath held by Bahadur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, a placeholder for the owner's shape while the occupation is drawn hatched: 'The whole of Gujarat, except Sorath, came under his [Humayun's] rule'.

correction.text: Gujarat after the loss of Malwa and Raisen in 1537: the mainland, Junagadh and Dwarka, without Bassein and Diu

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Bahadur Shah's death in 1537 Malwa is lost; the nobles carved the kingdom into feuding parts under Muzaffar Shah III (1561-1573), which the pages do not map.

region.text: the Gujarat plain around Patan, 'declared independence from the Tughlaq dynasty of Delhi'

ledger.note: 1394: Zafar Khan declares Gujarat independent of the Tughlaqs. Infobox 'Declared independence from Delhi Sultanate: 1394'; 'In 1392, he defeated Farhat-ul-Mulk in the battle of Kamboi'; the sultan's title and the rulers list begin with Muzaffar Shah I in 1407. The page gives no boundary.

region.text: Malwa around the capital Dhar, held by a Gujarat governor

ledger.note: 1407: Muzaffar Shah I enters Dhar and takes Malwa. 'In 1407, he reached the capital Dhar, where Sultan Hoshang Shah confronted him'; Hoshang was arrested, 'Malwa was annexed by Gujarat Sultanate' and 'Muzaffar appointed his brother Nusrat Khan to govern the territory' (infobox of the Gujarat page: 'Invasion of Malwa: 1407'). Drawn hatched because it lasted about two years.

region.text: Malwa around Dhar returns to Hoshang Shah

ledger.note: 1409: Hoshang Shah is restored in Malwa. The page gives no restoration year: 'Hushang Shah was released as situation went out of hands', after the Malwa nobles 'elected Musa Khan, Hoshang's cousin, as their leader by December 1408'; the infobox gives his reign from 1409.
1411: Ahmad Shah founds Ahmedabad and makes it the capital. 'Ahmad Shah laid the foundation of the city at the site of Asawal on 26 February 1411'; 'He chose it as the new capital on 4 March 1411.'

region.text: Idar in the north-east of Gujarat, captured in November 1428

ledger.note: 1428: Ahmad Shah captures Idar. 'He attacked Idar in 1425' and 'Ahmad Shah had to again attack and capture Idar in November 1428'.

region.text: Thane and Mahim on the Konkan coast

ledger.note: 1429: Gujarat attacks Thane. After the death of Kutub Khan, governor of Mahim, in 1429 Ahmad Shah 'attacked Thane by sea and land, captured it, and regained possession of Mahim'; the infobox of the Gujarat page dates the Konkan War 1429-1431.

region.text: Thane and Mahim

ledger.note: 1431: the Konkan War ends with Thane and Mahim in Gujarat's hands. Infobox 'Konkan War: 1429-1431'; 'Finally, Ahmad Shah annexed Thana and Mahim from Bahmani Sultanate'.

region.text: Thana and Mahim

ledger.note: 1431: Thane and Mahim annexed. 'Finally, Ahmad Shah annexed Thana and Mahim from Bahmani Sultanate' (the war ended 1431 by the infobox; the year of annexation is that of the war's end).

region.text: Khandesh under the Faruqis of Burhanpur, a tributary of Gujarat

ledger.note: 1437: Khandesh accepts Gujarat's suzerainty. 'Miran Adil Khan accepted the suzerainty of Gujarat sultanate' (1437); the Khandesh ruler had already sworn fealty after the siege of Thalner in 1417, and in 1498 'Gujarat army entered Khandesh', after which Adil Khan II 'agreed to pay the arrears' (the Mahmud Begada page: 'Mahmud reasserted Gujarat's suzerainty in 1500'). [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the Khandesh page gives no year for Miran Adil Khan's acceptance of Gujarat's suzerainty ('He accepted the suzerainty of Gujarat sultanate', in his reign 1437-1441); 1437 is his accession]

region.text: the Chudasama kingdom of Junagadh (Girnar) in Sorath

ledger.note: 1467: Mahmud Begada attacks Junagadh. 'In 1467, he attacked the fort of Junagadh' (Mahmud Begada page); infobox of the Gujarat page 'Conquest of Junagadh: 1467-1470'.

region.text: Junagadh

ledger.note: 1470: the conquest of Junagadh is complete by the Gujarat page's infobox; the Mahmud Begada page places the siege 'In 1472-73, after a siege of nearly two years', a disagreement between the pages.

region.text: Junagadh (Girnar) in Sorath

ledger.note: 1470: Junagadh annexed. 'Conquest of Junagadh: 1467-1470' (infobox); 'The conquest and annexation of Junagarh, Dwarka, and Champaner extended the frontiers of the kingdom' (Mahmud Begada page, which dates the siege 1472-73).

region.text: Dwarka at the western tip of Saurashtra

ledger.note: 1473: Mahmud marches on Dwarka. 'On 14 May 1473, Sultan Mahmud marched with a large army against Dwarka'; the page counts Dwarka among the annexed places but gives no later year.

region.text: Champaner and the fort of Pavagadh

ledger.note: 1483: Mahmud besieges Champaner. Infobox 'Siege of Champaner: 1483-1484'.

1484: the capital moves to Champaner. Infobox 'Champaner (1484-1535)'; the Mahmud Begada page also says that in 1479 he 'made the new city his capital under the name of Mustafabad' (Junagadh), which the Gujarat page's capital list does not carry.

region.text: Pavagadh and Champaner

ledger.note: 1484: Pavagadh falls on 21 November. 'Pavagadh was conquered on 21 November 1484.'

region.text: Champaner with the fort of Pavagadh

ledger.note: 1484: Champaner annexed and renamed Muhammadabad. 'Pavagadh was conquered on 21 November 1484' and Mahmud 'made it his capital under the name of Muhammadabad'.

region.text: the Malwa Sultanate of Mahmud Shah II

ledger.note: 1518: the Malwa sultan becomes Gujarat's vassal. 'Since 1518, Mahmud Shah II was a vassal of the Gujarat Sultan.' Rana Sanga's victory of 1519 and the annexation of 1531 follow.

region.text: northern Gujarat, annexed by Rana Sanga

ledger.note: 1519: Rana Sanga of Chittor defeats the joint army of Malwa and Gujarat. 'In 1519, Rana Sanga of Chittor defeated a joint army of Malwa and Gujarat sultanates'; 'Sanga also annexed northern Gujarat and appointed one of his Rajput vassals to rule there'. The page gives no year for the annexation and none for its end; the span is bridged to 1532, when Bahadur Shah first besieged Chittor.

region.text: Raisen, Bhilsa and Chanderi

ledger.note: 1531: Raisen, with Bhilsa and Chanderi, is taken. Raisen 'Captured in 1531 and placed under the governor of Malwa, Sultan Alam Lodhi, along with Bhilsa and Chanderi' (as read from the page); the former holder is not named in the extract.

region.text: Malwa

ledger.note: 1531: Gujarat annexes its vassal Malwa. Mandu fell on 28 March 1531 and 'Malwa was then annexed to his kingdom' (Bahadur Shah page).

region.text: Malwa, annexed to Bahadur Shah's kingdom

ledger.note: 1531: Mandu falls and Malwa is annexed. 'The fortress at Mandu fell and Sultan Mahmud and his seven sons were captured without any resistance on 28 March 1531'; the Malwa Sultanate page gives 25 May 1531 for the fall.

region.text: northern Gujarat

ledger.note: 1532: the Chittor campaign. Bahadur 'first besieged Chittor in 1532 and lifted the siege after receiving a large ransom'; the page is silent on what happened to northern Gujarat and by 1535 'The whole of Gujarat, except Sorath' is under the Gujarat king, so the contest is closed here as a bridging judgment.

region.text: Diu island and fort

ledger.note: 1534: the Portuguese hold Diu. The Bahadur Shah page says the Portuguese 'built the Diu Fort instead of the factory he had allowed them' and gives no year, so Diu is bridged to the treaty year; the Gujarat Sultanate page has 'In 1509, the Portuguese Empire wrested Diu from the Sultanate', which the Mahmud Begada page does not support (it dates only a naval battle).

region.text: Bassein, Bombay and Daman

ledger.note: 1534: Bahadur cedes Bassein to Portugal. 'On 23 December 1534 while on board the galleon St. Mattheus he signed the Treaty of Bassein'; 'the Portuguese Empire gained control of the city of Bassein'; the Gujarat Sultanate page adds that 'Bombay, Bassein and Daman would become a Portuguese colony'.

region.text: Gujarat except Sorath, and Malwa, in Humayun's hands

ledger.note: 1535: Humayun takes Mandu and Gujarat. 'Bahadur Shah, unaccustomed to defeat, lost heart and fled to Mandu, which fortress was speedily taken by Humayun'; 'The whole of Gujarat, except Sorath, came under his rule'; the Gujarat Sultanate page has Humayun attacking in 1535 'and briefly occupied it' (the same page gives 1532 once).
1535: the capital returns to Ahmedabad. Infobox 'Ahmedabad (1535-1573)'.

region.text: Gujarat and Malwa freed of the Mughals

ledger.note: 1536: Bahadur regains the kingdom. 'Bahadur Shah regained the kingdom in 1536' after the nobles drove the Mughals out when Humayun left to face Sher Shah Suri.

region.text: Malwa, partly regained by Qadir Shah

ledger.note: 1537: Malwa slips from Gujarat. Bahadur is killed on 13 February 1537 near Diu, and 'Qadir Shah, an ex-officer of the previous Khalji dynasty rulers, regained control over a part of the erstwhile kingdom' that year; the page gives no more.

region.text: Khandesh

ledger.note: 1573: the Gujarat suzerainty over Khandesh ends with the sultanate. The page gives no end for the relation; the last dated attestation is Miran Muhammad's joining of Bahadur Shah's campaign in 1532 and Miran Mubarak who 'signed a treaty with Gujarat' (undated), and Khandesh's next dated act is the annexation of Berar by Ahmadnagar in 1574.

region.text: Gujarat, taken from the nobles, the Mirzas and Sher Khan Fuladi

ledger.note: 1573: Akbar annexes Gujarat. 'Akbar annexed Gujarat in his empire in 1573' (infobox 'Annexed by Mughals: 1573'); 'Gujarat becoming the province of the Mughal Empire', the Gujarat Subah; Surat fell on 26 February 1573 and Akbar had reached the capital in November 1572 (Mughal conquest page).

wars.name: Gujarat-Malwa wars

zones.text: Malwa: Gujarat invaded in 1407, 1417, 1419, 1420, 1422 and 1438 and annexed it in 1531

wars.outcome: Gujarat occupied Dhar in 1407-1409, raided Malwa four times under Ahmad Shah I, and annexed it after Mandu fell in 1531; Malwa's own drive (with Khandesh) on Gujarat in 1417 failed.
wars.note: 'led four expeditions into Malwa in 1419, 1420, 1422 and 1438'; 'In December 1421, he advanced against Malwa and took the fort of Mesar' (Ahmad Shah I page). The Gujarat page's 1417 sentence: 'he invaded again in 1417 along with Nasir Khan'.

wars.name: Konkan War
wars.outcome: Gujarat annexed Thana and Mahim from the Bahmanis.
wars.note: The page also names Jhalawad as a party in the body text.

wars.name: Conquest of Junagadh
wars.outcome: Gujarat annexed Junagadh; the Mahmud Begada page places the siege at 1472-73.

wars.name: Siege of Champaner
wars.outcome: Pavagadh fell on 21 November 1484; Mahmud made Champaner his capital as Muhammadabad.

wars.name: Battles of Chaul and Diu
wars.outcome: A Portuguese naval victory at Diu in 1509 ('The Portuguese won the battle, and the event marks the start of European colonialism in Asia'); no land changed hands on the Mahmud Begada page.
wars.note: The Gujarat Sultanate page nevertheless says 'In 1509, the Portuguese Empire wrested Diu from the Sultanate'; the territory is dated 1534 (ledger, confidence 1).

wars.name: Rana Sanga's campaigns against Gujarat and Malwa
wars.outcome: Rana Sanga of Chittor defeated a joint army of Malwa and Gujarat in 1519 and annexed northern Gujarat.
wars.note: The page dates only the battle; the annexation and its end are undated.

wars.name: Humayun's invasion of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Humayun took Mandu and Gujarat in 1535 and withdrew in 1536 to face Sher Shah Suri; Bahadur regained the kingdom.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Akbar reached Ahmedabad in November 1572, took Surat on 26 February 1573 and annexed Gujarat as a Mughal province.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given for any frontier on the pages opened; the Bassein cession of 23 December 1534 names towns, not a boundary.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Cliopatria lacks the Gujarat Sultanate); the Delhi Sultanate umbrella and the Tughlaq shape of 1394 are the sa-04-b dossier's. Five Wikipedia pages plus two read for neighbours (Hoshang Shah, Khandesh Sultanate; Malwa Sultanate cited once). The Gujarat page gives no area, so every keyframe is a reading from the places the pages name; the extents are approximate.
Disagreements: Junagadh 1467-1470 (Gujarat infobox) against 'In 1472-73, after a siege of nearly two years' (Mahmud Begada); Mandu 28 March 1531 (Bahadur Shah page) against 25 May 1531 (Malwa page); Humayun 1532 or 1535 (Gujarat page); Mahmud made Junagadh (Mustafabad) his capital in 1479 on his page, against the Gujarat page's Ahmedabad 1411-1484; Diu 'wrested' in 1509 (Gujarat page) against a naval battle (Mahmud page).
Not settled: Nagaur's Rathods 'submitted' to Ahmad Shah in 1432 (a tributary, undated end, not drawn); Ranthambore taken shortly after 1532 (fort, not drawn); the nobles' partition of the kingdom under Muzaffar Shah III is undated; Ahmadnagar's acknowledgement of Bahadur as overlord (undated); the 1472 Sind and Kutch raid left no territory on the page; the 1519 annexation of northern Gujarat by Rana Sanga has no year or end on the page (contest 1519-1532 at confidence 1).
Counterparts needing a dossier: chudasama-dynasty (Junagadh to 1470), Champaner (Khichi Chauhans, Pavagadh to 1484), Idar. Mewar slug used: kingdom-of-mewar (successor of guhilas-of-mewar).
Gazetteer names needed: Champaner, Idar, Junagadh, Dwarka, Thane, Dhar, Raisen, Vasai (Bassein), Daman.
